subject: KineGrant: open action-authorization layer for physical AI (no-fee pilot)
body:
Hi FORT Robotics team,

I maintain KineGrant, an open-source action-level authorization and accountability protocol for robots and physical AI. Before an actuator moves, it requires a short-lived, one-time capability bound to the exact agent, target, action and purpose; after execution it produces a signed, hash-chained receipt for audit.

I'm reaching out because FORT focuses on exactly this problem - safety and security for intelligent machines - and KineGrant's open, vendor-neutral, post-quantum (ML-DSA-65) approach could complement your platform or serve as a reference implementation.

It's Apache-2.0, one-command install, with ROS 2 / Matter / OPC UA adapters and a zero-dependency offline browser verifier. OpenSSF Best Practices passing, Scorecard 7.7/10, Google OSS-Fuzz submitted.

Would you be open to a no-fee technical validation? A remote demo is enough to start.

Demo: https://kinegrant.com/playground.html
Source: https://github.com/zoahdev/kinegrant-protocol

Thanks,
KineGrant maintainer
